svg.title: How the terms of Traceworks lie inside one another
svg.desc: On the left, what an author writes: a package, a directory that holds scripts, rule files, container images, a catalog and optionally a seal, and a workflow. The workflow holds blocks, a block becomes steps, and each step runs in a container with one image, no network, a read-only workspace, a scratch folder and limits. The workspace, the project that is checked, belongs to neither side and is mounted read-only. An arrow named run leads to the right: package plus inputs plus workspace. On the right, what the tool keeps in the home: runs, each with its record, blobs, scratch and register folder; registers, one per audit, with findings, items and decisions; and the ledger, which holds the state of every run and register. A run of an audit reports to its register, and the next run reads it.
